name: Product reveal
what: One product, shown working or turning, with its price and how to order. The default for shops.

timeline.beat: The product already moving: in a hand, in use, or turning. No logo intro.
timeline.onScreen: The hook line, the price strip in the top third, the phone bar

timeline.beat: The product doing its job in close-up.
timeline.onScreen: One feature in 2 to 4 words

timeline.beat: Two more angles, colours or uses, 2 to 3 s each.
timeline.onScreen: One short label per shot

timeline.beat: The price card and what is included.
timeline.onScreen: Price in RWF in a solid box; the trust line if the owner gave one

timeline.beat: A clean hero shot of the product.
timeline.onScreen: The named route to order and the number, big, in the middle

text: The first line on screen at 0.0 s, about 5 words, upper-middle.
Spec words animate in one phrase at a time, white bold with an outline or in rounded boxes.
Never more than 2 lines of text at once.
voice: Optional. If used, it starts by 0.5 s, says the product, one benefit and the price as people say it (forty-eight thousand francs).
music: Upbeat and secondary to the voice; one whoosh or hit on the reveal.
cta: One route, named: 'WhatsApp {phone}', 'Call {phone}' or 'DM now before stock ends'.
eastAfrica: The price and the phone number are on screen from second 0 to the last frame.
Real hands, real shop shelves behind the product beat a blank studio for local trust.
A full address or landmark (T2000 House, Room 213B) makes a small seller credible.
Rwandan Facebook video ads run a median 34 s; for products and offers keep under 20 to 25 s.

name: UGC testimonial
what: A person (a customer, the seller or a presenter) finds, tries and recommends the product, filmed like a phone video.

timeline.beat: The person (or hands) in the real place with the POV or question line.
timeline.onScreen: The POV or question line, big, at the top

timeline.beat: They pick the product up and show it to the camera.
timeline.onScreen: Word-by-word captions of what they say

timeline.beat: They try it, use it or taste it; a real reaction.
timeline.onScreen: One benefit, in their words

timeline.beat: The product close to the lens.
timeline.onScreen: The price and what is included

timeline.beat: A smile and the product held up.
timeline.onScreen: The route to order and the number

text: Word-by-word captions are always burned in; most people watch muted.
Plain person-style words ('I found...', 'Nobody tells you...'), not slogans.
voice: First person, friendly, starts by 0.5 s. A fictional presenter never claims to be a real customer.
music: Light and low under the voice, or the room's own sound.
cta: Spoken and written: 'Order yours on WhatsApp {phone}'.
eastAfrica: A host who greets in Kinyarwanda ('Muraho') builds trust (on screen and in the caption; the voice speaks English).
Real customers eating or trying the product beat polished studio clips for local engagement.

name: Before and after
what: The result first, then how it was before, then the work, then the price and booking. For salons, cleaning, repair, renovation.

timeline.beat: The finished result, held still and bright.
timeline.onScreen: 'Wait for it...' or 'After'

timeline.beat: The before, dull and real.
timeline.onScreen: 'Before'

timeline.beat: Three quick process cuts or a time-lapse of the work.
timeline.onScreen: One step name per cut

timeline.beat: The full result again, held.
timeline.onScreen: The service name and the price

timeline.beat: The result with the business sign or the chair.
timeline.onScreen: 'Book: WhatsApp {phone}'

text: The 'After' or 'Wait for it...' line is the only text in the first 2 s.
Label Before and After plainly so a muted viewer follows.
voice: Optional; a short line on the result, then the booking line.
music: A beat with a hit on the reveal of the result.
eastAfrica: One flat price that includes a free extra (braids and a free wash) ran 982 days in Nairobi.
Never a body, skin or medical before/after (Meta and TikTok policy, owner rule).

name: Unboxing
what: Hands open the box; the item, its colour or its contents are the reward. No voice needed.

timeline.beat: The closed box in hands, top-down or POV.
timeline.onScreen: 'NEW IN' and the price

timeline.beat: The reveal: tape cut, lid off, one sound effect.
timeline.onScreen: Nothing, let the picture work

timeline.beat: The item turned: three angles or colours, 2 s each.
timeline.onScreen: One feature label per angle

timeline.beat: Everything that was in the box laid out.
timeline.onScreen: Price and 'what is in the box'

timeline.beat: The item held up next to its box.
timeline.onScreen: The route to order and the number

text: Little text during the reveal; the label and price come after it.
voice: None needed; if any, one excited line after the reveal.
music: A light beat; a whoosh or a pop on the opening.
cta: 'DM to order' or 'WhatsApp {phone}', plus delivery if the owner offers it.
eastAfrica: Boxes of new stock arriving is a credible 'new arrivals' story for Kampala and Kigali shops.

name: Tour
what: A walk through the place: a house, a venue, a restaurant, a shop, a fleet. Labels per space, then the price and the location.

timeline.beat: The best view or a whip pan into the best room.
timeline.onScreen: The location stack (city / area / street) and the key fact (4 BEDROOMS)

timeline.beat: The spaces one by one, 2 to 3 s each, smooth gimbal moves.
timeline.onScreen: One label per space (living room, kitchen, plot size)

timeline.beat: The outside or the view again.
timeline.onScreen: The price large ('400K RWF / month')

timeline.beat: The entrance or the sign.
timeline.onScreen: WhatsApp {phone}, the area and a landmark

text: Labels name each space; the price and the rooms are on screen in the first 3 s for property.
voice: A calm host or none; on Facebook a talking host can run 30 to 60 s.
music: Calm, warm; the room's own sound for restaurants.
cta: 'WhatsApp {phone}', the area, a landmark and the property ID if there is one.
eastAfrica: Kigali buyers filter on district, sector and size first: put them in the first 3 s.
The caption lists price in RWF, rooms, plot size, parking, the area and the number (Hills Props, Samkay).
Rwandan property ads: a yellow price box top-right ('350M RWF', 'Price: 16M') and a Kinyarwanda checklist caption; 30 s with an agent on camera.

name: Offer
what: One offer, loud and clear: a weekly deal, a promo price, a free extra. Ends with exactly how to get it.

timeline.beat: The product top-down or in a hand.
timeline.onScreen: The offer badge with the day ('BUY 1 GET 1 FREE', 'EVERY TUESDAY')

timeline.beat: A real person bites, opens or uses it.
timeline.onScreen: The badge stays

timeline.beat: A second item or a close-up.
timeline.onScreen: Its name and price next to it

timeline.beat: The place: the venue, the counter, the shop front.
timeline.onScreen: The area or the address

timeline.beat: The offer item again, clean.
timeline.onScreen: 'Order on {app}' or 'Call {phone}', in the middle

text: The offer is a solid badge that stays up; the same badge every week makes a series.
A percentage always comes with the real price ('37.5% off: 5K').
voice: The offer in one sentence, then the route to order.
music: Energetic; a drum hit on the badge.
cta: Named route: 'Order on VubaVuba', 'Call {phone}', 'WhatsApp {phone}', with the end date if there is one.
eastAfrica: Kigali restaurants run the same weekday offer every week (Tuesday pizza, Wednesday burger, lunch Monday to Friday).
'Hurry before the promo ends' only when the owner gave an end date.

name: 3D motion
what: The product floats under studio light with particles and giant type: a premium look from a product photo, no filming.

timeline.beat: A macro detail under a rim light (a cap, a label edge), particles drifting.
timeline.onScreen: One huge word or nothing

timeline.beat: The whole product floating in a themed set, ingredients or splashes around it, slow orbit or push-in.
timeline.onScreen: A giant word behind the product, cut by the frame edge

timeline.beat: One benefit per beat; the colour theme changes with each beat.
timeline.onScreen: 2 to 4 words, one key word highlighted

timeline.beat: The brand or price card on a clean background.
timeline.onScreen: Name or price in 3D; the number in a fixed lower-middle band

text: Giant words are part of the scene (behind or beside the product).
Even in 3D, the price label and the phone number appear for a Rwandan shop.
music: Cinematic or a clean beat; hits on each colour change.
cta: The brand card, then the number and the route.
eastAfrica: Premium 3D clips earned fewer local likes (3K to 7K) than real shops with real people: use 3D for premium products, and keep the price and the number in the motion.
On YouTube Shorts the craft clips (3D products, splashes, motion graphics) collect the likes (5K to 32K) while shop footage gets few: the clearest opening for the motion engine there.

name: Kinetic typography
what: Words carry the video: one phrase per beat, popping or stomping on the music, product photos flashing between.

timeline.beat: Two to four words stomp in on a solid colour.
timeline.onScreen: The hook, huge, one key word in the highlight colour

timeline.beat: One phrase per beat (0.5 to 1.5 s each), product photo flashes between phrases.
timeline.onScreen: 2 to 4 words per card

timeline.beat: The product photo with the price or the offer word.
timeline.onScreen: The price as the biggest word

timeline.beat: The route to order as the last card.
timeline.onScreen: 'WhatsApp {phone}'

text: One phrase at a time, 2 to 4 words, one highlighted key word.
Pop-in with overshoot or a slide with motion blur; hold each card 0.5 to 1.5 s.
A locked camera for text cards; a moving camera for products.
voice: None or a short tagline; the words are the message.
music: A strong beat: the words land on it.
cta: The last card is the route and the number.
eastAfrica: Use for launches and offers; keep the price and number as words in the motion.

name: Tutorial or expert talk
what: A named expert or teacher explains one thing in the real place, with boxed captions; proof, then how to book.

timeline.beat: The expert in the real place, or the promise of the lesson.
timeline.onScreen: Name and role card, or 'Don't say / Say'

timeline.beat: One problem, one explanation, step by step.
timeline.onScreen: Sentence-by-sentence boxed captions

timeline.beat: A result: a client, a before/after of the work (never a body), a certificate on the wall.
timeline.onScreen: One proof line

timeline.beat: The expert invites the viewer.
timeline.onScreen: Address, phone numbers, WhatsApp

text: Captions box each sentence as it is said: the video must work muted.
A red 'Don't say' and a green 'Say' is a before/after in one frame.
voice: The expert's own voice or a calm voice-over; one topic only.
eastAfrica: Derma Skin Clinic Rwanda runs 15+ variants of the doctor-explains format, in English and Kinyarwanda, with the address and two numbers in every caption.

name: List or price list
what: Several items, one per beat, each with its price; or the whole price list in one frame. Fast and practical.

timeline.beat: Item 1 already on screen (in a hand, or the full price list card).
timeline.onScreen: Number 1 or the list title, the phone number

timeline.beat: One item per beat, about 2 s each: a product in a hand in front of the stock, or one reason or lesson point.
timeline.onScreen: A big number and the item; a price label on each product

timeline.beat: The shop, the class or the team.
timeline.onScreen: 'Call / WhatsApp {phone}'

text: A price label on every item; the number never leaves the frame.
A full price list is a solid card that stays up long enough to read (or to screenshot).
voice: None, or each item and its price spoken.
music: A quick beat; one tick per item.
eastAfrica: Nairobi and Kampala sellers put a price on every product shot (150/=, KSH 35, 85,000) and keep the number on screen.
